note: The diagnostic registry for SiteSkin Manifest 1.0. Machine-readable so the conformance corpus can assert that every code has at least one fixture and every fixture code is registered. A code with no fixture does not exist.
layerOrderNote: The order validation runs in, and therefore the order in which a rejection short-circuits: a manifest rejected at one layer is never evaluated by a later one. Machine-readable because the corpus asserts against it — a fixture may not expect a diagnostic from a layer its own rejection has already made unreachable. See SPEC.md section 4.1.

layers.transport: Enforced on the response before the body is parsed.
layers.parse: Enforced while turning bytes into JSON.
layers.version: Enforced on a schemaVersion that is PRESENT and WELL-FORMED, after parsing and before schema validation. This layer has no opinion on an absent, non-string or malformed version — that is a structural defect and belongs to 'schema'. The split is real rather than a convenience: siteskin-1.0.schema.json validates the version *format* and deliberately does not pin the major, so an unsupported major is a policy rejection that no schema can express. It runs before 'schema' because a manifest declaring a major we do not know may legitimately have a structure this schema was never written for, and reporting a pile of structural errors against it would invite someone to handle them.
layers.schema: Enforced by siteskin-1.0.schema.json. Structural validity only — including the schemaVersion grammar itself.
layers.security: Enforced by the security validator. Not expressible in JSON Schema — these rules depend on the serving origin, which the schema does not know.

dispositions.reject: The whole manifest is discarded and the browser stays in regular mode.
dispositions.drop-item: The offending element is removed; the rest of the manifest still applies.
dispositions.warn: Nothing is removed; the diagnostic is recorded for the developer inspector.

diagnostics.summary: Manifest body exceeds 128 KB. Enforced before parsing, so an oversized payload is never fully read into memory.
Response body is not valid JSON.
schemaVersion declares a major version this implementation does not understand. Silently reinterpreting an unknown format is how a security boundary becomes a guess.
Document fails siteskin-1.0.schema.json: a missing required field, a wrong type, or a malformed value. Absence of a required field is not an element that can be dropped, so this rejects.

A URL resolves outside the serving origin. Not expressible in JSON Schema, which does not know the origin the manifest was served from — this is the rule that makes the schema/security split necessary rather than tidy.

A URI scheme outside the allow-list (https, mailto, tel, geo), or an external_url that is not HTTPS. Allow-list rather than deny-list: a deny-list is a bet that every dangerous scheme was enumerated, and intent: alone shows how that bet loses.

An asset URL lies outside the serving origin. Subdomains count as outside (ADR-004): a subdomain is frequently delegated to a third party, and inheriting the parent's branding would let that party impersonate it. The logo falls back to a monogram.

An action type outside the allow-list. Drops that item and keeps the rest of the manifest (ADR-007) — an E code that deliberately does not reject, which is why disposition is declared per code rather than inferred from the E/W prefix.

Two items in the same collection share an id. The FIRST occurrence wins and the later one drops, so the outcome depends on document order — an implementation using a last-write-wins map produces the opposite result.

A collection or string exceeded its limit and was truncated, keeping the first N in document order. Deliberately not enforced by the JSON Schema: a maxLength there would make an over-long title fatal, where SPEC.md section 8 requires it to be truncated.

A manifest colour failed WCAG AA against browser-owned text and was adjusted by the algorithm in SPEC.md section 9.1. The manifest colour moves, never the text colour — the text is the signal the correction exists to protect.

A field not defined in this schema version was ignored. Minor versions are additive, so unknown fields must never be fatal — this is the policy that lets a 1.1 manifest be served safely to a 1.0 reader. toolbar.showDomain reaches this path by design (ADR-006): it is ignored, not honoured.

An icon name the browser does not recognise; a generic glyph is substituted. Not a schema enum, because that would make a typo'd icon name discard the whole manifest — the same argument ADR-007 makes for unknown action types.
